text:
ConocoPhillips fell 5.2% today after reporting quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has been sliding since late October, losing nearly 6% over two weeks as oil prices have weakened—US crude is trading at $99.64 per barrel, down from the $150+ range seen just days ago. The earnings announcement and softer crude prices together triggered selling pressure in the energy sector.

The broader context adds weight to the decline: midterm election results have shifted political risk for oil majors, with Democratic control now favoring renewable energy investments over traditional oil and gas. While the sector faces a "demand decade" ahead according to recent executive commentary, near-term uncertainty about oil prices and geopolitical risk is keeping investors cautious on legacy energy stocks.
